description: The Indian Peafowl is a large, colorful bird known for its brilliant blue neck and long feather train. It is a symbol of beauty and grace in South Asia.
habitat: Forests, agro-forest areas, and village edges
diet: Seeds, insects, small reptiles, and plant matter
distribution: India, Sri Lanka, and parts of neighboring regions
interesting_fact: The male peacock displays its long tail feathers to attract females during courtship.

description: The House Sparrow is a familiar urban bird with crisp brown and grey plumage. It is highly social and often seen near homes and farms.
habitat: Urban areas, villages, and agricultural lands
distribution: Across Europe, Asia, and parts of North America
interesting_fact: House Sparrows often live close to humans and are known for forming large communal flocks.

description: The Common Kingfisher is a small bird with brilliant blue upperparts and a sharp, pointed beak adapted for catching fish.
interesting_fact: This bird often perches above water and dives quickly to catch prey with remarkable precision.

description: The Barn Owl is a nocturnal bird of prey recognized by its pale face, heart-shaped facial disc, and silent wingbeats.
habitat: Open countryside, barns, agricultural fields, and grasslands
interesting_fact: Barn Owls can hunt in near darkness using extremely sensitive hearing.

description: The Rock Pigeon is a familiar city bird with gray plumage, a small head, and a strong homing instinct.
habitat: Cities, cliffs, buildings, and agricultural regions
diet: Seeds, grains, and small plant matter
interesting_fact: Domestic pigeons are descendants of the wild Rock Pigeon and are known for their navigation abilities.

description: This parakeet has a bright green body, a rosy collar, and a strong hooked bill used to crack seeds and fruit.
distribution: South Asia and introduced regions in Africa and Europe
interesting_fact: They are highly vocal and often gather in noisy flocks during the evening.

description: The Common Myna is a bold and adaptable bird with dark brown plumage, a bright yellow bill, and a loud call.
habitat: Urban centers, agricultural regions, and open areas
diet: Insects, fruits, seeds, and garbage scraps
distribution: South Asia and many introduced areas across the world
interesting_fact: Common Mynas often imitate sounds and can be highly visible around human settlements.

description: The Indian Roller is known for its vivid blue-green wings and graceful aerial displays. It is often seen perched on power lines.
habitat: Open countryside, grasslands, and agricultural land
distribution: South Asia and parts of Southeast Asia
interesting_fact: Their display flight is dramatic, showing a brilliant burst of color when they dive and turn.

description: This bulbul has a compact body, a black head, and a vivid red patch under the tail. It is common in gardens and scrubland.
habitat: Shrubland, gardens, forests, and urban green spaces
interesting_fact: It produces a cheerful and repeated song that is often heard in the early morning.

description: The Black Kite is a graceful raptor often seen soaring over cities and open fields while scanning for food.
habitat: Open country, wetlands, towns, and agricultural landscapes
diet: Small mammals, fish, birds, and carrion
interesting_fact: Black Kites are opportunistic feeders and can often be seen gliding in search of food.
